author: EmuCore - Hub
title: PCSX2 gives GameDB families a shared source of compatibility fixes
summary: Standard YAML anchors let regional, demo, and promotional SKUs reuse a named fix set, extend it, or override one field instead of copying large blocks that later diverge.
heroAlt: Visual evidence from PCSX2 pull request #14649: Add support for YAML anchors in GameDB

sourceLabels.pcsx2-pr-14649: Add support for YAML anchors in GameDB

blocks.text: Copied GameDB blocks made related discs drift apart

PCSX2's GameDB contains many SKUs of the same title, each with serial-specific metadata and compatibility settings. Gran Turismo alone has more than seventy entries. When identical gsHWFixes blocks are copied into every SKU, a later correction can reach one region but miss a demo or promotional disc. Pull request #14649 addresses the data model rather than adding another script that tries to keep copies synchronized.
Anchors support direct reuse, expansion, and field-level override

A fix map can now be named with a YAML anchor and referenced unchanged by another serial. A later entry can merge that map, add recommendedBlendingLevel, and expose the expanded result as a second anchor. Another SKU can inherit that result and override halfPixelOffset while preserving the remaining fixes. Clamp modes can follow the same pattern, allowing shared behavior and genuine disc differences to remain visible in one entry.
Declaration order is enforced by the existing YAML toolchain

YAML aliases may only refer to anchors already declared earlier in the file. That limitation is not hidden: the GameDB linter is expected to catch a forward reference. Support was added through common/YAML and GameDatabase rather than a PCSX2-specific text substitution, so the stored document remains standard YAML. Reviewers can read where a value originates instead of deciphering a separate inheritance language.
Gran Turismo is both the migration and the regression suite

Validation must load representative Gran Turismo serials from each inheritance level: a direct alias, an expanded Prologue set, and a GT4 entry overriding halfPixelOffset. The emulator should report the same effective fixes that the duplicated entries provided before migration. The linter should reject an alias moved before its declaration, and a local override must change only the named field. That combination checks syntax, merge order, and compatibility behavior.
The benefit is editorial correctness in compatibility data: one shared fix can be improved once, while explicitly different SKUs keep their documented overrides.
